name: Shaphat
overview: Shaphat was a male leader from the tribe of Gad, recognized as the second chief in the region of Bashan. His role as a Gadite chief highlights his position of authority within this tribe. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphat means 'he judges,' reflecting a role or characteristic associated with judgment or leadership. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 5:12 and was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Shaphat is explicitly identified as a descendant of Gad, linking him directly to the tribe of Gad. Beyond this tribal relationship, Scripture does not record any further family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphat's significance in Scripture derives from his leadership role as the second chief in Bashan, a position of considerable responsibility among the Gadites. This indicates his importance in the governance and military organization of his tribe during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles. His mention underscores the structured leadership within the tribes of Israel.
